cards.explanation: The anterior pituitary depends entirely on portal delivery of hypothalamic hormones, so cutting that supply starves it of CRH and ACTH output drops. Cortisol feedback is not removed here, since cortisol falls once ACTH falls. Axonal delivery serves the posterior lobe, and the corticotroph does not release much ACTH without CRH drive.

cards.q: Thyroid hormone rises well above normal in a healthy person given an injection. Predict what happens to TSH and to TRH.
cards.a: Both fall, because long loop feedback inhibits both tiers above.
options: TSH rises and TRH falls, because feedback acts only on the hypothalamus
Both rise, because more substrate is available for the axis
Both fall, because long loop feedback inhibits both tiers above
TSH falls and TRH rises, because only the pituitary senses thyroid hormone
cards.explanation: Long loop feedback from the third tier reaches both upstream tiers, so a rise in thyroid hormone suppresses TRH and TSH together and secretion of new thyroid hormone slows. A rise in all three would be positive feedback, which is not how this axis works. The two split answers each assume feedback lands on only one tier, but the long loop targets both.

cards.q: A tumor secretes ACTH continuously and is not part of the pituitary. Predict what happens to CRH from the hypothalamus.
cards.a: CRH falls, suppressed by both the high cortisol and ACTH.
options: CRH is unchanged, since the tumor is outside the axis
CRH rises, because the adrenal gland is being overdriven
CRH rises to match the ACTH output
CRH falls, suppressed by both the high cortisol and ACTH
cards.explanation: High ACTH drives cortisol up, and cortisol suppresses the hypothalamus by long loop feedback while ACTH itself suppresses it by short loop feedback, so CRH is doubly inhibited. Rising CRH would require the feedback signals to be stimulatory. The tumor is outside the normal axis but its hormone is not, so the loops still respond.

cards.q: A patient takes a high dose of a synthetic glucocorticoid for months. Predict the state of CRH, ACTH, and the adrenal cortex.
cards.a: CRH and ACTH are low and the adrenal cortex atrophies.
options: CRH and ACTH are low and the adrenal cortex atrophies
CRH is high, ACTH is low, and the cortex is normal
CRH and ACTH are low and the adrenal cortex enlarges
CRH and ACTH are high and the adrenal cortex enlarges
cards.explanation: The drug acts on the same receptors as cortisol, so the axis reads it as an excess and shuts down both upper tiers, and without ACTH the cortex loses its trophic support and shrinks. High CRH and ACTH would require the axis not to recognize the drug. A cortex cannot enlarge while its trophic hormone is suppressed, since ACTH is what maintains its mass.

cards.q: Which observation would be evidence of short loop feedback rather than long loop feedback?
cards.a: Infusing ACTH into the hypothalamus lowers CRH with cortisol held constant.
options: Infusing cortisol lowers ACTH release from the anterior pituitary corticotrophs
Infusing ACTH into the hypothalamus lowers CRH with cortisol held constant
Removing the adrenal glands raises ACTH
Infusing cortisol lowers CRH release from the hypothalamus
cards.explanation: Short loop feedback is the trophic hormone acting on the tier above it, so showing an effect of ACTH on CRH while cortisol is clamped isolates that loop. Infusing cortisol and watching either ACTH or CRH tests the peripheral hormone acting upstream, which is the long loop. Removing the adrenals raises ACTH by removing cortisol feedback, which is again the long loop.

cards.q: GnRH is given as a steady continuous infusion instead of in pulses, and LH output falls after a few days. What best explains the fall?
cards.a: Continuous exposure down regulates GnRH receptors on the gonadotroph.
options: GnRH becomes an antagonist when given continuously
The hypothalamus stops making GnRH by short loop feedback
Continuous exposure down regulates GnRH receptors on the gonadotroph
Continuous exposure destroys the hypophyseal portal vessels over time
cards.explanation: The gonadotroph needs a pulsatile signal, and unrelenting stimulation causes receptor down regulation so the same hormone level does progressively less, which is the basis of using GnRH analogs to suppress the axis. The portal vessels are not damaged by hormone exposure. GnRH does not change into an antagonist, and suppressing hypothalamic GnRH would not matter when GnRH is being infused from outside.

cards.q: Growth hormone acts partly through IGF-1 made in the liver. Which molecule provides the long loop negative feedback on the hypothalamus and pituitary in this axis?
cards.a: IGF-1.
options: Somatostatin
Insulin
GHRH
IGF-1
cards.explanation: IGF-1 is the peripheral product of the axis, so it plays the role cortisol or thyroid hormone plays elsewhere and inhibits both GHRH release and growth hormone release. GHRH is the tier one releasing hormone rather than a feedback signal. Somatostatin is an inhibiting hormone from the hypothalamus, part of the control rather than the feedback from the periphery, and insulin belongs to a different regulatory system.

cards.q: A researcher cuts the pituitary stalk in an animal. Predict what happens to cortisol and to antidiuretic hormone over the following week.
cards.a: Cortisol falls with the loss of ACTH drive, and antidiuretic hormone release is impaired too.
options: Cortisol falls with the loss of ACTH drive, and antidiuretic hormone release is impaired too
Cortisol is unchanged and antidiuretic hormone falls, since only the posterior lobe uses the stalk
Cortisol falls and antidiuretic hormone rises, since the posterior lobe is released from inhibition
Both cortisol and antidiuretic hormone rise, since feedback pathways are cut
cards.explanation: The stalk carries both the portal vessels to the anterior lobe and the axons to the posterior lobe, so one cut interrupts hormonal delivery on one side and neural delivery on the other. Neither hormone can rise, since both depend on structures the cut removes. The anterior lobe is not spared, because its entire hypothalamic input arrives through those portal vessels.

cards.q: Both adrenal glands are removed from an animal. Predict CRH, ACTH, and skin pigmentation over the following weeks, and explain the link.
cards.a: CRH and ACTH rise as feedback is lost, and high ACTH darkens the skin.
options: CRH and ACTH fall, and the skin becomes pale from low ACTH
CRH and ACTH rise as feedback is lost, and high ACTH darkens the skin
CRH rises and ACTH falls, and pigmentation is unchanged
CRH and ACTH are unchanged, since the axis senses only the pituitary
cards.explanation: Cortisol is what normally restrains the upper two tiers, so removing its source releases both from inhibition and ACTH climbs, and because ACTH is derived from the same precursor as melanocyte stimulating hormone it darkens the skin at high levels. A fall in the upper tiers would require more cortisol, not less. CRH and ACTH move together here, since the same feedback loss reaches both.

cards.q: An animal is given a drug that blocks the glucocorticoid receptor everywhere. Predict CRH, ACTH, and plasma cortisol after several days.
cards.a: All three rise, because the axis cannot sense the cortisol that is present.
options: CRH and ACTH fall while cortisol rises, because feedback is amplified
All three fall, because the receptor block prevents hormone release
All three rise, because the axis cannot sense the cortisol that is present
CRH and ACTH rise while cortisol falls, because the adrenal is blocked too
cards.explanation: Feedback works only if the upstream tiers can detect the hormone, so blocking the receptor makes cortisol invisible to the hypothalamus and pituitary and they drive the axis harder, raising all three measured values. A fall in all three would follow extra feedback rather than none. The adrenal cortex itself is not blocked, so it responds to the rising ACTH by making more cortisol.

cards.q: TRH is infused into a healthy person for one hour. Predict the sequence of changes in TSH and thyroid hormone, and what finally limits the response.
cards.a: TSH rises first, thyroid hormone follows, and the rise then shuts off TSH.
options: TSH and thyroid hormone rise together and stay high until the infusion ends
TSH falls while thyroid hormone rises, because TRH inhibits the pituitary
Thyroid hormone rises first, then TSH follows, and TRH runs out
TSH rises first, thyroid hormone follows, and the rise then shuts off TSH
cards.explanation: Signals move down the axis in order, so the pituitary responds within minutes and the thyroid takes longer, and once the peripheral hormone is up it uses long loop feedback to restrain TSH even while TRH is still arriving. The peripheral hormone cannot lead its own trophic hormone. A sustained plateau would require feedback to be absent, and TRH stimulates the pituitary rather than inhibiting it.

cards.q: In endocrine disease, what does the word primary tell you about where the defect is?
cards.a: The defect is in the peripheral gland itself.
options: The defect is in the peripheral gland itself
The defect is in the anterior pituitary
The defect is in the target tissue receptor
The defect is in the hypothalamus
cards.explanation: Primary points to the last tier of the axis, the gland that makes the hormone with the body wide effects, so the tiers above it are healthy and still responding to feedback. A pituitary defect is called secondary and a hypothalamic defect is called tertiary. A receptor defect in the target tissue is hormone resistance, which is a separate category from primary and secondary.

cards.q: In endocrine disease, what does the word secondary tell you about where the defect is?
cards.a: The defect is in the anterior pituitary, so the trophic hormone is abnormal.
options: The defect is in the peripheral gland, so the trophic hormone is abnormal
The defect is in the anterior pituitary, so the trophic hormone is abnormal
The defect is in the target tissue, so the receptor is abnormal
The defect is in the carrier protein, so the free fraction is abnormal
cards.explanation: Secondary names a problem one tier up from the peripheral gland, at the anterior pituitary, so the trophic hormone is the thing that is wrong and the peripheral gland is merely following orders. A defect in the peripheral gland itself is primary. Receptor and carrier protein problems change how hormone acts or travels rather than which tier of the axis is broken.

cards.q: What happens to TSH in primary hypothyroidism?
cards.a: It is high.
options: It is normal
It is undetectable
It is high
It is low
cards.explanation: The thyroid gland is failing, so thyroid hormone is low, and low thyroid hormone removes the long loop inhibition on the pituitary, which pushes TSH up. Low or undetectable TSH would mean the pituitary is the failing tier, which is secondary hypothyroidism. A normal TSH with a low thyroid hormone is not what an intact feedback loop produces.

cards.q: What happens to TSH in secondary hypothyroidism?
cards.a: It is low, because the pituitary is the failing tier.
options: It is high, because feedback is lost
It is normal, because only the thyroid is abnormal
It is high, because the thyroid is not responding
It is low, because the pituitary is the failing tier
cards.explanation: In secondary disease the pituitary cannot make enough TSH, so the thyroid is understimulated and thyroid hormone falls with it, leaving both tiers low. A high TSH with low thyroid hormone is the primary pattern, in which the pituitary is healthy and shouting at a broken gland. Saying only the thyroid is abnormal describes primary disease, not secondary.

cards.q: What happens to ACTH when an adrenal tumor secretes cortisol on its own?
cards.a: It is suppressed.
options: It is suppressed
It is unchanged
It rises and then plateaus
It is elevated
cards.explanation: The tumor makes cortisol without waiting for orders, and the high cortisol feeds back on the pituitary and hypothalamus, so ACTH is pushed down even while cortisol is high. Elevated ACTH with high cortisol would mean the pituitary is the source of the problem. Feedback is intact here, so ACTH cannot stay unchanged or drift upward.

cards.q: What happens to ACTH when a pituitary tumor secretes ACTH on its own?
cards.a: It is high, and cortisol is high too.
options: It is low, and cortisol is high
It is high, and cortisol is high too
It is high, and cortisol is low
It is low, and cortisol is low as well
cards.explanation: The tumor is at the trophic tier, so it floods the adrenal cortex with ACTH and the cortex responds by making more cortisol, leaving both tiers high. Low ACTH with high cortisol is the adrenal source pattern. High ACTH with low cortisol would mean the adrenal cannot respond, and both low is pituitary failure rather than a secreting tumor.

cards.q: Why is measuring the peripheral gland hormone alone not enough to classify a disorder as primary or secondary?
cards.a: Both patterns give the same peripheral level, so the trophic hormone decides.
options: The peripheral hormone is bound to protein, so it cannot be measured
The peripheral hormone is too unstable to measure accurately in plasma
Both patterns give the same peripheral level, so the trophic hormone decides
The peripheral hormone changes only in secondary disease, never in primary
cards.explanation: A low thyroid hormone looks identical whether the thyroid failed or the pituitary failed, so the tier above is what tells you which one broke, which is why these values are always read as a pair. The peripheral hormone can be measured reliably, and protein bound hormones are routinely assayed as free or total. The peripheral hormone changes in both primary and secondary disease, which is exactly the problem.

cards.q: What does the term hypersecretion mean in this classification scheme?
cards.a: Too much hormone is being released, whatever tier is at fault.
options: The target tissue is unable to respond to a normal hormone level
The hormone is released at the wrong time of day
Too little hormone is being released from the peripheral gland
Too much hormone is being released, whatever tier is at fault
cards.explanation: Hypersecretion and hyposecretion describe the direction of the abnormality, while primary and secondary describe its location, so a full classification uses one term from each pair. Too little hormone is hyposecretion, the opposite direction. Failure of the target tissue to respond is resistance, and abnormal timing is a separate problem from the amount released.

cards.q: A patient has a low free T4 with a high TSH. Classify the disorder.
cards.a: Primary hyposecretion.
options: Primary hyposecretion
Secondary hypersecretion
Secondary hyposecretion
Primary hypersecretion
cards.explanation: Low peripheral hormone sets the direction as hyposecretion, and the high trophic hormone shows that the pituitary is healthy and pushing hard on a gland that cannot answer, which places the defect in the thyroid itself. Secondary hyposecretion would show a low TSH alongside the low T4. Both hypersecretion answers are ruled out because the peripheral hormone is low, not high.

cards.q: A patient has a high free T4 with a suppressed TSH. Classify the disorder.
cards.a: Primary hypersecretion.
options: Secondary hyposecretion
Primary hypersecretion
Secondary hypersecretion
Primary hyposecretion
cards.explanation: High peripheral hormone sets the direction as hypersecretion, and the suppressed trophic hormone shows the pituitary is responding normally by shutting down, so the thyroid must be making hormone on its own. Secondary hypersecretion would show TSH high or inappropriately normal despite the high T4. Both hyposecretion answers are ruled out because the peripheral hormone is high.

cards.q: A patient has a high free T4 together with a high TSH. Classify the disorder.
cards.a: Secondary hypersecretion.
options: Secondary hyposecretion
Primary hypersecretion
Secondary hypersecretion
Primary hyposecretion
cards.explanation: Hormone is high, so the direction is hypersecretion, and the striking finding is that TSH is high when feedback should have shut it off, which means the pituitary is driving the thyroid rather than obeying it. Primary hypersecretion would show a suppressed TSH, since the healthy pituitary would respond to the excess. Both hyposecretion answers contradict the high peripheral hormone.

cards.q: A patient has a low free T4 together with a low TSH. Classify the disorder.
cards.a: Secondary hyposecretion.
options: Primary hyposecretion
Secondary hypersecretion
Primary hypersecretion
Secondary hyposecretion
cards.explanation: Low peripheral hormone gives the direction, and a low trophic hormone in the face of it is the giveaway, since a healthy pituitary would have raised TSH sharply. Both tiers falling together points to failure at the pituitary. Primary hyposecretion would show a high TSH. The hypersecretion options do not fit a low peripheral hormone.

cards.q: A patient has a low morning cortisol with a markedly elevated ACTH. Where is the defect and in which direction?
cards.a: The adrenal cortex, with hyposecretion.
options: The adrenal cortex, with hyposecretion
The adrenal cortex, with hypersecretion
The anterior pituitary, with hypersecretion
The anterior pituitary, with hyposecretion
cards.explanation: Cortisol is low, so the direction is hyposecretion, and the elevated ACTH proves the pituitary is working and being ignored, which places the failure in the cortex itself. A pituitary defect would leave ACTH low along with cortisol. Neither hypersecretion answer is possible when the peripheral hormone is low.

cards.q: A pituitary tumor destroys the corticotrophs while sparing the adrenal glands. Predict the ACTH and cortisol levels and classify the result.
cards.a: Both low, secondary hyposecretion.
options: ACTH high and cortisol low, primary hyposecretion
Both low, secondary hyposecretion
ACTH low and cortisol high, primary hypersecretion
Both high, secondary hypersecretion
cards.explanation: Losing the cells that make ACTH removes the trophic drive, and an adrenal cortex that is intact but unstimulated makes very little cortisol, so both tiers read low and the defect is one tier above the gland. High ACTH with low cortisol would require a healthy pituitary and a failing adrenal. The two options with a high hormone contradict the loss of secretory cells.

cards.q: Which pair of values is impossible in a patient whose feedback loop is intact and whose only problem is in the peripheral gland?
cards.a: High peripheral hormone with high trophic hormone.
options: Low peripheral hormone with a trophic hormone at the top of its range
Low peripheral hormone with high trophic hormone
High peripheral hormone with high trophic hormone
High peripheral hormone with low trophic hormone
cards.explanation: If the pituitary is healthy it must suppress the trophic hormone when the peripheral hormone is high, so seeing both high means the trophic tier is the driver and the problem is not confined to the peripheral gland. Low peripheral with high trophic and high peripheral with low trophic are the two normal responses of an intact pituitary to a failing or overactive gland. A trophic hormone at the top of its range alongside a low peripheral hormone is simply an early or mild primary deficiency.

cards.q: Two patients both have a plasma cortisol far above normal. Patient A has a suppressed ACTH and patient B has a high ACTH. Classify each and name the tier at fault.
cards.a: Patient A has primary hypersecretion from the adrenal cortex, patient B has secondary hypersecretion from the pituitary.
options: Both have primary hypersecretion, since cortisol is high in each
Both have secondary hypersecretion, since ACTH controls cortisol in each
Patient A has secondary hypersecretion from the pituitary, patient B has primary hypersecretion from the adrenal cortex
Patient A has primary hypersecretion from the adrenal cortex, patient B has secondary hypersecretion from the pituitary
cards.explanation: An identical peripheral value carries opposite meanings depending on the tier above it, so the ACTH is what separates the two: suppressed ACTH means the pituitary is correctly reacting to an adrenal source, while high ACTH means the pituitary is the source and the adrenal is obeying. Reversing the two is the commonest error and comes from reading the peripheral hormone alone. Grouping them together ignores the trophic values entirely.

cards.q: An animal has a low thyroid hormone level. Exogenous TSH is given and thyroid hormone rises normally. Which tier was at fault, and what would the result have been in the other case?
cards.a: The pituitary was at fault, since the gland responds when stimulated. A failing thyroid would not.
options: The pituitary was at fault, since the gland responds when stimulated. A failing thyroid would not
The hypothalamus was at fault, since TSH bypasses the pituitary and the thyroid alike
Neither tier was at fault, since exogenous hormone always raises the level
The thyroid was at fault, since the gland needed extra stimulation. A failing pituitary would not have responded
cards.explanation: Supplying the missing trophic hormone tests whether the peripheral gland is capable, so a normal rise proves the thyroid is healthy and the shortage was upstream, which is secondary hyposecretion. A gland destroyed by primary disease would stay flat no matter how much TSH arrived. TSH does bypass the hypothalamus, but a hypothalamic defect would also have left TSH low before the test, so this result alone does not point there, and saying that exogenous hormone always raises the level ignores that a damaged gland cannot respond.

cards.q: A patient has low cortisol with low ACTH, low thyroid hormone with low TSH, and low sex steroids with low LH. What single lesion explains all three axes, and how do you know it is not three separate gland failures?
cards.a: One anterior pituitary lesion, since three failed glands would each raise their trophic hormone.
options: Three separate peripheral gland failures, because each peripheral hormone is low
One anterior pituitary lesion, since three failed glands would each raise their trophic hormone
One peripheral gland lesion, because the pituitary controls all three glands from one cell type
A carrier protein deficiency, because all the measured hormones travel bound
cards.explanation: Every trophic hormone is low alongside its peripheral partner, which is the pattern of a pituitary that cannot drive any axis, and it is the low trophic values rather than the low peripheral values that make the call. If the three glands had each failed on their own, feedback would have pushed TSH, ACTH, and LH high. One peripheral lesion cannot explain three different glands, and carrier protein loss would not lower the trophic hormones.

cards.q: A young athlete takes large doses of a synthetic androgen. Predict the plasma testosterone, the LH, and the size of the testes, and explain the pattern.
cards.a: Measured androgen activity is high, LH is suppressed, and the testes shrink from lost trophic support.
options: Androgen activity is high, LH is unchanged, and the testes are unchanged
Androgen activity is high, LH is high, and the testes enlarge
Androgen activity is high, LH is suppressed, and the testes shrink
Androgen activity is low, LH is suppressed, and the testes are unchanged
cards.explanation: The drug acts on androgen receptors, so the hypothalamus and pituitary read the axis as oversupplied and shut down LH, and without LH the testis loses its trophic support and atrophies, which reproduces the high peripheral with low trophic pattern of a source outside the axis. High LH alongside high androgen would mean the pituitary was driving the excess. LH cannot stay unchanged with an intact feedback loop, and the androgen effect is clearly high rather than low.
